items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: To have four trombones was a luxury in those days unless you were Basie or Lunceford or Duke or what not.

ctx.x: It was economics, obviously. To have four trombones was a luxury in those days unless you were Basie or Lunceford or Duke or what not. But, yeah.
And you did your first recordings with Benny Carter?

items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Jay, can you recall the reaction to that first solo with him? What was it? The King? I can’t remember if that was it. [INTERVIEWEE] It may have been The King.

ctx.x: [laughs] It worked. It worked like a charm.
